_evidence: 0x00518654 (starts the three ramps of a sound channel; compose after chan_005188f5, whose 16-entry channel arrays and mask 0x88f704 (u16, both bit states for the bts/btr CF) it reuses): 'mov eax,[0x88f6cc]; mov ebx,[eax*4+0x88f998]' indexes the 100-entry sample->channel map with the current sample (0..99, the map's size, see chan_005188f5), and the map entry is the channel k: the bit offset of 'bt [0x88f700],ebx' / 'bts|btr [0x88f704],ebx' and the index of the 16-dword arrays ([ebx*4+0x88f708..0x88f908]), so 0..15 (the scanners loop k < 0x10). The enable mask 0x88f700 is mostly 0xffff with mixed patterns so both bt outcomes occur. For each ramp 'mov edx,[target]; mov [k*4+targetarr],edx; sub edx,[k*4+cur]; je' and otherwise 'shl eax,2; cdq; idiv dword [0x88f6dc]': the divisor (the ramp time) is nonzero ({1,2,3,7,0x40,-1,-5,0x1000}; zero faults) and the dividend is at most 4*0x8100 in magnitude, so every quotient fits. The three targets 0x88f6d0/d4/d8 and the three current arrays 0x88f708/0x88f788/0x88f748 (overriding chan_005188f5's wide ranges) are drawn from the same small set {0 (3/4), 0x100, -0x8000} so each 'je' goes both ways and all three deltas are zero together (ebp stays 0: the btr path) in about a fifth of the cases.
